messages:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH - Auth token reuse spike detected. 8k 401/429s in last 6m, unusual egress to s3://external-logs-uploads. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/auth-spike

sam (oncall): Ack. I'm on it. pulling ingress logs now. any immediate customer reports? :eyes:

cs-ops: No direct customer pings yet. One CS ticket flagged increased error rate for embeddings endpoint, linking to sample request IDs.

anya (infra): I can see repeated PUTs from a service account `svc-logger-prod` to that external bucket. Source IPs look like our logging fleet IPs. Checking instance metadata and recent deploys.

mike (eng-sre): If that's real, we should cut egress from logging fleet to S3 while we triage. Propose adding a temporary deny rule on the egress SG and rotate the svc-logger key.

lee (security): Agreed. Prioritize key rotation + egress block. Potential data exposure: logs in that bucket — start indexing to know what was sent (PII? tokens?). IR please prep legal/notify plan.

ir-team: On it. Start collecting timestamps and example object keys. We'll need an artifacts list for potential disclosure notice.

sam (oncall): Status: running `grep` on recent logs for `Authorization:` leaks and searching KV cache traces. If we find token headers sent, treat as secret exposure.

anya (infra): Quick mitigation commands:
```
# block egress from logging fleet
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-logging --protocol -1 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0 --rule- - # placeholder
# rotate service key
aws iam update-access-key --access-key-id AKIAxxxx --status Inactive --user-name svc-logger-prod
```
I'll run sanitized commands and post results.

mike (eng-sre): I'll prepare a short-lived deny on the egress LB to that bucket and deploy a config to stderr-warn if any app tries to write to external S3.

cs-ops: If customer impact appears, we should create a single comms bridge and assign one CS rep to own messaging. Tentative ticket created CS-789.

lee (security): Can engineering confirm whether those log writers had permission to include request headers in log payloads? That would explain auth tokens in artifacts.

anya (infra): Early sample shows full request body for some endpoints got included. Looks like a misconfigured log serializer introduced in last release to `log-level: debug` for embeddings path. Rolling that config back now.

sam (oncall): OK — immediate actions: 1) block egress (anya), 2) rotate svc-logger credentials (anya + mike), 3) roll back debug logging (mike), 4) run search for tokens in bucket and if found, mark as exposed (lee + ir-team). Assigning owners in incident doc.

ir-team: We found ~120 objects with potential tokens. Pulling object list and snapshots. Starting an export to secure bucket for analysis.

lee (security): If tokens are confirmed, rotate all affected service tokens and issue forced session invalidation for user tokens in that time window. Prioritize keys that grant write access.

mike (eng-sre): I've deployed egress deny, confirmed S3 PUTs stopped. Rotating svc-logger creds now. Will push a hotfix to remove debug logging.

cs-ops: Notifying a small set of customers whose request IDs appear in the leaked objects. Draft message ready — awaiting legal.

sam (oncall): Update: mitigation in place, blocking + rotation + rollback. Investigations team to continue object review. Will keep pager open until confirmation of no further exfil. :white_check_mark:

pagerduty-bot: Incident severity updated to P2 (mitigating). Next update in 30m or on significant change.

lee (security): Next steps: full token rotation list, audit of logging serializer change, internal postmortem once stabilized. Adding owners and timeline to the incident doc.

mike (eng-sre): Leaving a short note in ops channel and following up with deployment diff.

cs-ops: Customer comms queued pending legal. Standby for templates.

sam (oncall): Handoff: I'm stepping off in 15m. Anya will take primary oncall. Please escalate to me if anything reopens. :wave:
